Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 62, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Jumu'ah (Friday), because it mentions the day of Friday, its prayer, and explains some of the rulings and virtues of this day.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• Honouring the Messenger (ﷺ) and his mission, for through him Allah rescued the Arabs from the darkness of shirk, and through him He honoured humanity.

• Discussing the Jews and their deviation from the Shariah of Allah, and refuting their claim that they are the friends (awliya') of Allah. The surah presents an example of them: the donkey that carries large, beneficial books on its back, yet gains nothing from them except fatigue and toil, which is the ultimate of wretchedness and misery.

• Mentioning a number of the rulings concerning the Friday prayer (salat al-Jumu'ah).

[The Tafsir]

Everything in the heavens and everything on the earth glorifies Allah, exalting Him above everything that does not befit Him. He alone is the Owner of all things, the One who disposes of them without any contender, the One exempt from every deficiency, the Mighty (al-'Aziz) who cannot be overcome, the Wise (al-Hakim) in His management and His creation.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 62, verses 2–3:

Allah, glorified is He, is the One who sent among the Arabs, who could not read and who had no scripture and no trace of a message with them, a Messenger from among them to all people. He recites to them the Qur'an, purifies them from corrupt beliefs and bad morals, and teaches them the Qur'an and the Sunnah. Indeed, before his mission they were in clear deviation from the truth. He, glorified is He, also sent him to other people who have not yet come, and they will come from among the Arabs and from others. Allah, the Exalted, alone, is the Mighty, who prevails over everything, the Wise in His sayings and His deeds.

This is the commentary on 62:4 from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar:

"That sending of the Messenger (ﷺ) among the Arabs and others is a bounty from Allah, which He gives to whomever He wills of His servants. And He alone is the Possessor of great kindness and abundant giving."

The likeness of the Jews, who were charged with acting upon the Torah and then did not act upon it, is like the likeness of a donkey that carries books without knowing what is in them. Evil is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of Allah and did not benefit from them. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people, who transgress His limits and go out of His obedience.

Say, [O Messenger], to those who have adhered to the distorted Jewish faith: If you claim falsely that you are the beloved of Allah to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death, if you are truthful in your claim that Allah loves you.

This is a commentary passage on the verse, not the verse itself in the usual ﴿ ﴾ form, so I translate the commentary text directly.

And these Jews will never wish for death, out of preference for the worldly life over the Hereafter, and out of fear of God's punishment for them, because of the disbelief and evil deeds they have committed before. And God is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers; nothing of their wrongdoing is hidden from Him.

Say: "Indeed, the death from which you flee is unavoidable, for it will come to you when your appointed terms arrive. Then you will be returned, on the Day of Resurrection, to Allah, the One who knows the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of your deeds and will recompense you for them."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 62, verse 9:

O you who have believed, Allah and His Messenger, and acted according to His law: when the call to prayer is proclaimed for the Friday prayer, then proceed to hear the sermon and perform the prayer, and leave off trade, and likewise buying, and everything else that preoccupies you from it. That which you have been commanded is better for you, because in it is the forgiveness of your sins and the reward of Allah for you, if you know the benefits for yourselves, then do that. And in the verse is evidence for the obligation of attending the Friday prayer and listening to the sermon.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 62, verse 10:

Then when you have heard the khutbah (sermon) and performed the prayer, disperse throughout the land and seek Allah's provision through your effort, and remember Allah often in all your circumstances, so that you may succeed in attaining the good of both this world and the Hereafter.

When some of the believers saw a trade or some of the amusement and adornment of this world, they scattered toward it and left you, O Prophet, standing on the pulpit delivering the sermon. Say to them, O Prophet: What is with Allah of reward and bounty is better for you than amusement and trade, and Allah alone is the best of those who provide and give, so ask Him, and seek help through obedience to Him in attaining what He has of the good of this world and the Hereafter.
